outcome.description: You broadcast on the same frequency: 'I've backed up everything I know to three separate locations. Anything happens to me, it goes public.' Silence. Then a single ping. The shadow vessel's engines flare and it breaks off pursuit, jumping to transit. You've bought yourself time, but the message is clear: The Ledger knows your name, and they're not afraid to show it.

Your sensors strain against the vessel's emission dampeners, but you manage to pull a partial hull signature. The alloy composition matches Guild military construction: not a converted freighter, but a purpose-built surveillance ship. Someone with access to Guild shipyards had this vessel constructed off the books. You store the signature data alongside your growing evidence file.

You alter course to a busy trade lane and lose yourself in commercial traffic. The shadow vessel doesn't follow. Or at least, you can't detect it anymore. For the next few days, you stick to routine trading runs and keep your head down. But the data you've collected doesn't delete itself.

Director Voss reviews your records with practiced efficiency. After several minutes, she nods. "Your accounts are in order. The Bureau appreciates your cooperation, and I have noted your compliance in our files."

Director Voss pauses, then concedes the point. "You are within your rights, of course. I will note that you requested counsel and schedule a formal review at Nexus Prime. Good day." She cuts the channel. The audit is delayed, but not forgotten.

Director Voss's expression hardens. "I will note your refusal in the Bureau's records. I trust you understand the implications for your standing with the Commerce Guild." The cutter peels away without another word.

You authorize the payment, and the enforcement officer logs your compliance. "Your tariff receipt has been filed. You are cleared to proceed. The Commerce Guild thanks you for your contribution to regulated trade." The frigate moves on to its next target.

You cite corridor jurisdiction precedents from the Bureau's own charter. There is a long silence before the officer responds. "Your objection has been noted and will be reviewed by the Bureau. You may proceed. For now." No credits change hands.
The enforcement officer's tone shifts from bureaucratic to cold. "Noncompliance noted. Enforcement protocols are now in effect." The frigate's weapon ports begin to glow.

Inspector Holloway's team scans every container and cross-references serial numbers. Eventually, he declares your cargo compliant. "Everything appears to be in order. You may proceed." His disappointment is audible.

Holloway glances at his crew, then back at you. "An expedited review can be arranged for a standard facilitation fee." The credits vanish into what is almost certainly not an official Bureau account, and Holloway waves you through with suspicious efficiency.

Holloway's jaw tightens. "Refusal to comply with Bureau Directive 4412 constitutes obstruction of regulated commerce. I am authorized to enforce compliance." His vessel's weapon arrays begin their targeting sequence.

Gil's scanner sweeps your ship in seconds. 'Clean as creek water. Appreciate the cooperation, Captain.' His wingmate tips a salute. 'You see anything suspicious out there, broadcast on channel seven. We'll come running.'
Gil frowns but nods. 'Your right, Captain. Just know that folks who refuse scans tend to get remembered out here. Fly safe.' The patrol logs your transponder ID as it moves on.

Gil's eyes light up. 'Now that's useful. We been tracking a pattern but missing a piece. This fills the gap.' He transmits a small bounty from the patrol's community fund. 'You ever need a favor out here, you got friends on channel seven.'
The officer scans your documents and nods to herself. 'Everything checks out. Safe travels, Captain.' The cruiser peels off and resumes its patrol route.

The officer warms up once your papers clear. She mentions increased raider activity two systems over and flags a few safe waypoints on your chart. 'Watch yourself out there,' she says before signing off.
The officer shares tactical data: raider positions, ship profiles, their preferred ambush points. You update your nav charts with safe corridors.
The officer raises an eyebrow but doesn't refuse. You join a short-range sweep that flushes out a raider scout. The patrol commander logs your contribution and transfers a bounty payment.
You log the advisory and tighten your route planning. The patrol frigate resumes its sweep as you push deeper into the lane.

You transmit every official document in your ship's database. The drone processes them for eleven minutes, then responds: 'Form 27-B/6 not found. However, your filing of seventeen unrelated forms has earned you Provisional Existence Status, valid for ninety days. Please file Form 27-B/6 before expiry to upgrade to Confirmed Existence. Have a productive cycle!' It flies away.

The drone considers your offer. 'Expedited processing is available for a nominal fee of 30 credits.' You pay. The drone stamps your transponder signal with something called a 'Certificate of Probable Existence' and departs. The certificate gets you a 5% discount at Guild administrative offices.
You hit the throttle. The drone pursues for exactly twelve seconds, broadcasting 'Your unauthorized existence has been noted!' before returning to its patrol route.

You power down and drift with the picket ships. Roz sends over a thermos of coffee via drone. Strong enough to strip hull paint. 'You're alright,' she says. The strike settles after a few hours, and the Union remembers who stood with them.

Roz chews it over. 'You ain't Deep Core, I'll give you that. Alright. Go around the back side, quiet-like. And if anyone asks, you never saw us.' She transmits an alternate route through the asteroid scatter.
You gun the engines and thread through the formation. Roz's voice follows you, cold as vacuum: 'We'll remember that, Captain. We remember everything.' The Union won't forget this insult easily.

Cal boards with a clipboard older than your ship and proceeds to find seventeen 'violations,' most of which are judgment calls at best. But he also catches a hairline crack in your secondary coolant line that could've blown next week. 'See? That's why we do this.' He waives the fines and patches the crack himself.

Cal stares at you for a long moment. 'I'm gonna pretend I didn't hear that, on account of you probably not knowing how things work out here. We don't do that.' He inspects your ship twice as thoroughly. You pass.

Cal scratches his jaw. 'Technically true. But technically, my friends on the dock can take real long processing your cargo next time you're in Breakstone. Your call.' He lets you pass, but makes a note on that clipboard.

You work alongside the Okafor team, using your ship's systems to help map the contamination spread while their drones deploy sealant charges. Dr. Mwenzi is brisk but grateful: 'Your thermal imaging data saved us approximately three hours of sweep time. The Okafor Institute does not forget those who assist in public health emergencies.' She authorizes a field stipend from the Institute's emergency fund.

You adjust course without argument. Dr. Mwenzi notes your compliance with a brief acknowledgment: 'Thank you for your cooperation. The diversion adds approximately twelve minutes to standard transit. We anticipate clearing the quarantine within forty-eight hours.'

The Okafor frigate tracks you with its sensor array as you attempt to bypass the zone. Dr. Mwenzi's voice turns cold: 'Quarantine violation logged. Your transponder has been flagged. I strongly advise against exposure to the contaminant. Symptoms include progressive neural degradation.' You clear the zone, but not without consequence.

The detour costs you time, but a Guild logistics officer notices your compliance and pings a small fuel credit to your account. "Appreciate the cooperation, Captain. Half the independents out here try to barrel through."
You catch fragments of an encrypted debate: something about tariff adjustments and a 'Forge Sector proposal.' You log the fragments. A patrol vessel gives you a long look before moving on.
You angle away from the restricted zone.

You maintain position for forty minutes. The unclassified energy signature pulses twice more, then fades. The all-clear comes through with no further explanation. A Collective patrol ship sweeps past your position, sensors clearly scanning you, before moving on.

Your sensors capture fragmented data before a Collective patrol ship moves to block your line of sight. The readings are strange: energy patterns that don't match any known reactor type or weapon system. The patrol captain sends you a terse warning: "Cease unauthorized scanning." But the data is already in your logs.
You plot a course out of Axiom space and don't look back until the station is a dot on your rear sensors.

You send your credentials, manifest, and destination without argument. The patrol officer reviews them line by line, then: "Credentials verified. You are cleared to transit Corridor 7-Alpha. Maintain heading and speed. Deviation will be treated as hostile intent." The drones peel off.

You cite Union-recognized transit rights and refuse the full manifest disclosure. The patrol officer pauses. They know the regulations. "Fine. Credentials and destination only. But we're logging this interaction, Captain." You transit without the invasive cargo scan, but DCMC has your name on a list now.
You transfer a quiet credit bundle to the patrol officer's personal account. The targeting lock drops immediately. "Cleared for transit. Have a productive day, Captain."

You transmit your credentials and state you're passing through on a trade route. The synthesized voice processes this for five seconds. "Acknowledged. Maintain your declared heading. Do not deviate. Do not scan." The patrol ship holds position as you pass, its sensors tracking you until you're out of range.
You transmit a confident Guild transit authorization. The patrol ship pauses, then: "Authorization noted. Proceed to Corridor 3. Do not access station approach vectors." They let you through.
You don't argue. You throw your engines into reverse and back out of the sector. The patrol ship watches you go without comment.
